answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The sable multiplier is published, charged in ridge, and crystal lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 964 identities would post 1688 proofs and burn roughly 15 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
